{"self_assessment": "Impact
I kept the table supplied so the builders never had to stop for dominoes. I made three trips to the boxes, 40 dominoes each, 120 in total, into the shared bin at roughly 0:45, 1:45 and 3:00. The bin was at 52 at one point and stayed stocked for the rest of the build. The fish was fully connected, with all 113 standing dominoes dark from the start, and it was finished with time to spare.

Execution
I chose the biggest batch size per trip. A 40-domino trip costs about 60 seconds, against 46 seconds for just 12, so each domino cost far less travel time. I told the table the bin level so nobody had to guess, and I stopped fetching once the bin was clearly enough, so no one lost time to unnecessary trips. I didn't place any dominoes myself.

Collaboration
I backed Jack's fish idea straight away and said clearly that I'd be on supply, so everyone knew the bin was covered. I posted the bin count and my next trip so the builders could plan around it. Once the run was connected, I agreed with the hands-off call so nothing got bumped before the push.

Leadership
I took ownership of a job nobody else was doing and kept it going without being asked. I made the supply plan visible to the table, and I called the last 'fingers off' before the push.

I think supply was a real part of this result, because the builders could work continuously. But the shape, the lines and the joins were built by Hana, Jack and Omar, and I only supplied them.", "my_share_percent": 25}
